articleTitle: Selection of evaluation criteria for finishing subcontractors for small construction companies
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Construction is one of the most important areas in global development, which is constantly changing in the way of work, one of the most notable is the practice of outsourcing activities known as subcontracting. This work model can carry out up to 90% of the project with high percentages concentrated in the finishing stage due to the need for specialization and practicality in its development. However, in the context of small, combined construction companies, the evaluation of subcontractors focuses clearly on the "lowest bid budget" that is made, leaving aside technical aspects relevant to the success of the project. Considering the above, the research focuses on defining the evaluation criteria that allow reducing risks and increasing the probability of complying with the triple restriction of scope, cost and time of the projects. To do this, the corresponding literature was reviewed, and surveys were carried out with professionals related to subcontracting corresponding to the double filter of the Delphi technique. Finally, they were grouped following qualification parameters, obtaining 7 criteria with their respective weights as the most influential: Experience, Quality, Financial capacity, Security, Production, Communication and Offered cost

articleTitle: Colour recognition algorithm for an inclusive experience (July 2018)
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This study focused on developing a colour recognition algorithm in such a way as to privilege accuracy and efficiency without losing information in the images and evaluating colour detection techniques based on RGB space. The proposed approach combines colour detection techniques with the introduction of optimised parameters, comparing it with two traditional colour identification algorithms. A method involving image pre-processing and machine learning algorithms is employed, enhancing the images with matching and filtering techniques to increase the accuracy of colour detection.

articleTitle: Proposal of Redesign of Data-based Lean Management- Oriented Business Processes in the Textile Industry: Previous Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This study addresses productivity challenges in Peruvian textile SMEs, focusing on limited machine availability, high failure rates, and lack of standardized processes. These issues lead to defective garments and high reprocessing rates, impacting productivity. A Lean Manufacturing model incorporating 5S, Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), and process standardization was implemented. Data on machine availability, failure rates, and reprocess percentages were collected and analyzed to measure the model's impact. The Lean Manufacturing model significantly improved productivity, achieving 0.25 units/sol. Machine availability increased, and reprocesses were reduced by 20%, demonstrating the model's effectiveness. This research provides a novel application of Lean Management, integrating data management and analytics to enhance productivity in textile SMEs. It offers valuable insights into 5S, TPM, and process standardization, contributing to both academic literature and industry practices.

articleTitle: Interpretation of the sedimentation process in the proposed sand trap of the Cerro del Aguila dam
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: According to the ISI Program (International Sediment Initiative), it is mentioned that erosion and sedimentation processes in the management of water bodies, such as the Cerro del Aguila reservoir, is a very important issue on a worldwide scale from a social, economic and environmental point of view [1]. The desander projected for the Cerro del Aguila reservoir is a large-scale one that would provide an important improvement in the management and care of the dam's infrastructure. With the proposed improvement of the geometry of the proposed desander for the Cerro del Aguila dam, it is expected to obtain a considerable optimization in the operation and projected efficiency of the sand trap, as well as with respect to the operating flow requirement of the turbine of the power plant, which is one of the weak points of the initial proposed design. The verification of the functionality of the proposed improvement evidences as a consequence, the opportunity of implementing a "Flushing" type washing system with Bieri type purge gates, which results in a second advantage offered by the improvement regarding the optimization of the operation in general. As numerical results of the modeling considering a particle size of 0.5 mm, we have, on the one hand, a velocity of 0.11 m/s (low velocities), and on the other hand, that the amount of sediments deposited in a year within the 3 vessels for a flow rate of 70 m3/s is a total volume of 0.01 Hm3, without decreasing the operational flow of the turbine. This large amount of sediments can be removed automatically and efficiently, reducing plant shutdowns for maintenance, operating costs and losses due to power outages, as well as extending the useful life of the expensive electromechanical installations. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Improvement model applying Holt-Winters and 7's method to reduce waste and production time in the Peruvian gastronomic sector
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: SummaryThe main objective of this study is to analyze the possibility of reducing input waste and the preparation time of fresh dishes, thus reducing the impact of costs with a sustainable approach based on a forecast method (HoltWinters) and a lean tool (7'S); which can be applied in cafeterias, restaurants and/or other food establishments. The company under study presented a generation of input losses of 14%. In comparison, the company's target is 10%. In relation to the production time of fresh plate, the object of study presented an average of 18 minutes per plate. In comparison, the company's goal and accepted by the public is 15 minutes. leading to a monetary loss of $3,281.16. To reduce the impact of the problem, we used the Holt-Winters method for demand forecasting and 7'S, which reduced the percentage of shrinkage to 4% and fresh dish preparation times to 14 minutes. These results were obtained in a pilot test carried out lasting 1 month in the company. The investment for the proposed model would be $84.73, and the financial analysis shows that the project is profitable since the NPV after implementation is $4,928.64. It can be concluded that the model proposal positively impacts the results of the company under study.

articleTitle: Methodologies for the design of semi-rigid pavements with granular materials treated with cement: a review
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The use of granular materials treated with cement MGTC increases the structural capacity and durability of pavements. The design of pavements using these materials contemplates fatigue damage in the asphalt mix, cracking of the MGTC and rutting in the subgrade. This document aims to analyze the methodologies used for the design of flexible pavements considering MGTC. To this end, the math fundamentals, procedures and formulations of the Australian methodology (AUSTROADS), South African Pavement Design Method (SAMDM) and American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) are exposed. Likewise, the criteria used by the Urban Development Institute IDU for the city of Bogotá in Colombia are exposed. From the bibliographic review carried out, the authors present some comments and suggestions for the design of pavements in Colombia.

articleTitle: Management Model Based on the Croston Method and Nash-in-Nash Negotiation to Increase Sales in a Small Hardware Business
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Companies in the hardware and home improvement sector have experienced an increase in Peru, driven specifically by the sale of hardware products. This has led to increased competitiveness, requiring companies to manage their resources and strategies promptly to achieve a positive impact on their sales and, consequently, their market profitability. In this context, this research work aims to increase the sales of a small hardware business (SME) located in the Lima district through the implementation of the Croston method and Nash-in-Nash negotiation. This hardware store experienced a 44% decrease in sales from 2021 to 2022. Indicators were also established to measure the impact of the proposed tools on the processes to be improved and on the company's sales. As a main result, an increase in sales of 6.39% was achieved, demonstrating the effectiveness of the implemented model.

articleTitle: Integrated Lean Warehouse – DDMRP Model to Reduce Non-Fulfillment of On-Time Deliveries at the Metalworking Company U.S. ITEM S.A
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The metalworking sector contributes 11.2% to the manufacturing sector and represents 1.4% of the national GDP. The trade within this sector grew by 21.6% in 2022; for this reason, the following article is based on the import and commercialization of metallurgical products by U.S. ITEM S.A., located in Lima, Peru. The importance of the service level is crucial for generating optimal profitability as it reduces costs associated with non-compliance; therefore, it is essential to properly plan requirements, warehouse order, and correct execution in order preparation. For this reason, the study was conducted in the warehouse area of the Chesterton product line. The application of 5S, SLP, ABC Classification, EOQ, and MRP tools was proposed to improve the on-time delivery (OTD) indicator, which due to insufficient warehouse management stands at 64.53%. By implementing a pilot plan and performing a simulation in Arena, in addition to generating a simulated model applying hypothesis analysis, the improvement of the OTD indicator by 12.58% was verified with the proposed model.

articleTitle: Implementation plan to increase sales using CRM and Inbound Marketing for a microenterprise in the cultural and arts sector
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: In the new scenario that the country faced, the business sector underwent many changes, and one of the most affected were Peruvian SMEs. As a result, total sales of Peruvian SMEs decreased by 59.2% in 2020 compared to the previous year. The present article is in the cultural and arts sector, where it is evident that the SME experiences a decrease in profitability, low digital sales, and poor customer relationship management. In response to this, the objective of this research is to develop a methodology to increase the e-commerce of an SME in the cultural and arts sector. The methodologies to be implemented are the CRM model, which uses process digitalization, and at the same time, Inbound Marketing to increase profitability, digital sales, and ensure proper customer relationship management.

articleTitle: Proposal for improving product Delivery Times through the Standard Work Tools, TQM and the Sweep Method in a company in the Logistics Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This research work focuses on analyzing how the implementation of management tools can contribute to improving delivery times in a company in the logistics sector. The study company presented an average delivery time of 3.15 days, compared to the standard of 3 days. This is caused by incorrect distribution of products (64.72%), non-standardized processes (22.58%) and defective products (12.9%). To reduce the impact of the problem, TQM, Standard Work and the sweep method will be used, which will reduce delivery times by 33%. These results were validated using the Arena simulator, thus giving a final average of 2.12 days in terms of delivery time. Likewise, the investment for the proposed model would be 14,930 PEN, and the financial analysis shows that the project is profitable since the IRR (45%) is greater than the COK (15.62%) and has a positive NPV. It can be concluded that the initial proposal positively impacts the company’s results.

articleTitle: A Management Model to Increase Sales in a Small Hairdressing Business Based on 5S and BPMN
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The project titled "A Management Model to Increase Sales in a Small Hairdressing Business Based on 5S and BPMN" proposes a systematic approach to improving the business operations of a small hairdressing company. The project employs the 5S methodology, a Japanese approach to quality management based on five principles: Seiri (sort), Seiton (set in order), Seiso (shine), Seiketsu (standardize), and Shitsuke (sustain). This approach is used to improve workplace organization, operational efficiency, and thus, productivity. Additionally, the project uses Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN), a business process modeling technique that allows for the graphical and standardized visualization of business processes. BPMN is used to identify and optimize key processes that affect the company's sales and profitability.

articleTitle: Aplication of Circular Economy to Manufacture Sneakers from The Banana Pseudostem Yarn
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Traditional sneaker production uses water and soil contamination, due to the use of synthetic fibers and bad waste management. But new solutions have been developed, one of them being the replacement of natural fiber for synthetic fiber, one of the natural fibers is the banana fiber obtained from the pseudostem using mechanical machinery. The purpose of this article is to prove the feasibility of using mechanical and classical procedures to make sneakers but using banana fiber as the main resource by creating a prototype. The prototype will be tested in a laboratory and have these results: flexural strength with no appreciable damage. The rub fastness result is dry 5 and wet 5. The thickness of the sole is 19.4 mm. The Sole flexural strength does not have signs of damage, and the resistance of the shear-floor joint is 8.9N/mm.

articleTitle: Model to Reduce Waste Levels by Applying the 6'S Methodology in a Food Distribution Company
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Despite the implementation of methodologies such as Kaizen and Lean in various industries and companies of different sizes, the food industry worldwide continues to experience a concerning increase in food waste. The motivation for this study lies in the lack of specific solutions and the innovative focus on a small company. A model based on the 6'S methodology, centered on organization, order, cleanliness, safety, standardization, and discipline, is presented to reduce waste in the process of selecting and loading merchandise. The 15-day pilot test reduced damaged products due to rough handling and cross-contamination by 47.82% and 61.96%, respectively. Despite the process time increasing by 20.86%, these results meet the study's objective of reducing waste levels in the small food industry company in Peru.

articleTitle: Application of the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) tool, the ABC method, and the implementation of the Scrum methodology to increase the sales of a small outdoor advertising company
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: In the following case study, three processes were analyzed: sales process, after-sales process, and inventory management with the aim of increasing sales in an outdoor advertising company. This is explained in the evidence obtained throughout the project; for example, the number of lost customers, the lack of training for employees, and the number of supplies that were understocked. Additionally, the main problems identified in the case study were the lack of digital advertising services, inadequate after-sales processes, and inventory management. Therefore, as a proposed solution, a model based on the Scrum methodology, the CRM tool, and the ABC method was implemented, which efficiently implemented a new service, standardized the after-sales process, and improved the inventory management process of the company studied.

articleTitle: An Analysis of WELL Building Standard in South America
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: In recent years, attention has been paid to health and wellness in buildings, as people spend most of their time at work and in their homes. In that context the WELL Building Standard has emerged as a key solution to promote health and wellness. However, there is a lack of knowledge in developing countries about its implementation. That is why the objective of the following article is to analyze the adoption of the WELL Building Standard in South America and to evaluate the number of projects in this region. For this purpose, the projects in the WELL Building Standard database are evaluated. After initial review 310 projects are identified and finally fifteen projects certified were identified in South America, of which twelve are in Brazil and the rest are in Peru, Chile and Colombia. In addition, in South America the majority of certified projects have obtained the platinum level with nine certified projects, the gold level with four projects and the silver level with two projects. The following research will be a contribution for professionals and academics who wish to implement the WELL Building Standard.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Impact of Expanding a Cycling Network on Crossing Times and User Interactions at an Intersection in Metropolitan Lima
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Currently, there is a significant number of conflict points at intersections with bike lanes involving various users, whether motorized vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians. Additionally, with the exponential growth of the population and poor traffic culture, this insecurity intensifies and increases delay times. Hence, the need arises to find an analytical method capable of quantifying road safety, particularly for cyclists, and addressing a greater number of variables integrally. Such is the case at the intersection of Salaverry and Cuba avenues in the city of Lima, where Salaverry Avenue has a bike lane in the central berm of its roadway section.With this objective in mind, two scenarios were analyzed: Scenario A without the expansion of the bike lane on Cuba Avenue, and Scenario B with the expansion of the bike lane on said avenue. The focus was on evaluating the incidence of conflict points and delay times by sectors in both scenarios. Subsequently, in Scenario B, where fewer conflict points were identified, various traffic flows were analyzed, and the relationship between delay times was found.

articleTitle: Redesign of Data-based Lean Management-Oriented Business Processes in the Textile Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of improving delivery times in the textile industry, focusing on a company in Peru with a current on-time delivery rate of 76.92%. The goal is to enhance delivery performance through a data-driven redesign of business processes. We collected data via semi-structured interviews, direct observations, and production records up to 2022. Based on these findings, an integrated model utilizing Single-Minute Exchange of Die (SMED), 5S, and Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) was developed. The study identified key issues, including machine downtime and process inefficiencies, contributing to delays and implementing the proposed model improved process efficiency and delivery times, confirming the effectiveness of integrating SMED, 5S, and TPM tools. This research provides a novel approach by combining multiple quality improvement methods to address delivery issues, offering practical insights for continuous improvement and sustainability in the textile industry

articleTitle: Application of 5S, Standardized Work, and Heijunka to Increase Productivity in A Peruvian Packaging SME
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The objective of the research is to improve the productivity of an extra virgin olive oil bottling plant to meet its demand. The initial diagnosis of the company's situation was carried out, revealing three main causes for its issues, leading to the application of lean tools. The 5S implementation was used to clean and organize the production area, the simulation of Standardized Work addressed the lack of task assignment by optimizing the production flow through the efficient implementation of work sheets for operators, and the simulation of Heijunka was used to reduce the frequency of production changes due to a lack of production planning. The results obtained with Minitab Statistics software were evaluated after the implementation, comparing the indicators with the initial state of the company. The results show a 32% increase in productivity. Furthermore, the process changeover time decreased by 71%, and the bottle waiting time for each activity was reduced by 18%. It is important to mention that this work serves as a reference for future research and for replication in similar companies.

articleTitle: Sustainable Value Proposition Model Canva: Methodology for the Design of a Sustainable Food Business Project aimed at reducing the consumption of trans-fat products in preschool children in Metropolitan Lima using the DT Method and Sustainable Business Model Canva tools
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, there has been an 80% increase in the excessive consumption of trans-fat products, negatively impacting the diet of preschool children; understood as infants aged between 3 and 5 years old. Packaged processed snacks with warning labels have become an ally for parents responsible for planning their children's meals, as they simplify the process of packing lunches or providing snacks in their daily routine. This has resulted in the development of cardiovascular, neurological, endocrine, and other pathologies that affect their quality of life, indicating a cause-and-effect relationship. At the end of 2021, Consumer Protection Commission No. 3 conducted a study in which 45 snacks were selected to assess whether they complied with established fat limits. Of these, only 5 passed the test, which is not only concerning but also infuriating. Hence, a quantitative study is proposed to contribute to a solution to the identified need in the food sector, ensuring it is sustainable, nutritious, and healthy for the target audience. This study employs a combination of the Sustainable Business Model Canva and the fourth phase of the DT Method (Value Proposition Canva) to design a value proposition with the characteristics mentioned before. Finally, validation is carried out through Hedonic Testing (facial and acceptance).

articleTitle: Proposal for an Improvement Model to Reduce Aircraft Spare Parts Overstock Based on ABC Methodology and Neural Network Forecasting in an Air Service Company in Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The problem of overstock of aircraft spare parts is a critical challenge faced by the aviation industry in Peru. Inefficient management of spare parts demand can lead to unnecessary costs and a lack of vital parts, jeopardizing operational safety. The importance of addressing this issue lies in ensuring safety and economic efficiency in the sector. Despite previous efforts by other authors in this field, the solution proposed in this article stands out for its innovative approach. As students of Business Management Engineering, our personal motivation lies in seeking practical solutions for real business challenges like the one presented. This article provides an approach that combines neural networks to forecast spare parts demand with the ABC methodology to ensure effective inventory classification. The main result of this successful implementation is a substantial improvement in the accuracy of demand forecasts. Additionally, the application of this technology and methodology in spare parts management is a fundamental step in addressing the overstock problem, enhancing operational efficiency and safety in the aviation industry.

articleTitle: Project for the implementation of a lean startup business model to reduce STEM education gaps through an Arduino-based robotics course and co-creating
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Currently, Peru invests 19.5% of the national budget in education, reflecting a 16.9% improvement compared to 2022. However, these efforts take time to be applied in the areas of Science (STEM), an educational area that requires the greatest investment due to its experimental nature. In Metropolitan Lima, this is particularly noticeable in vulnerable populations, even though they are so close to the central government. Therefore, solutions are needed to address this gap. Most private companies providing education are disconnected from the reality of these populations, offering solutions that do not meet the economic and social needs of the users. While there are already various social assistance organizations, most of them do not have the necessary tools to provide high-impact solutions on their own. Hence, the purpose of this research is to propose a business model that allows considering social impact factors while facilitating the creation of companies or ventures capable of offering solutions to address this gap. During the development of this document, a "Lean Social Entrepreneurship Canvas" was created by combining relevant methodologies. This model was subsequently evaluated by social assistance organizations already operating in Lima. The interest of these organizations, and the fulfillment of the proposed indicators, validates the model.

articleTitle: Machine Learning models for predicting academic withdrawal in college students
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This study compares several binary classifiers for predicting the academic withdrawal of university students taking mathematics subjects in the first semester. The Random Forest model, using k-fold cross-validation and the SMOTE balancing technique, was found to be the most effective. The most influential variables for the prediction of academic withdrawal included taking the first semester mathematics course, the faculty to which the students belonged, and the professional orientation received before entering university. The Random Forest model showed a good fit, efficiently classifying students' non-continuation, allowing better control of critical variables such as teaching methods, professional orientation and accompaniment strategies, which can decrease dropout and increase academic success indicators. The variable "taking the first semester subject" was the most significant predictor, highlighting the importance of understanding mathematics in academic success. The variable "Faculty" suggests reviewing the dropout conditions by faculty, especially in Economics, where the highest percentage of academic withdrawal is presented (8.79%). The "Professional orientation" was also a determinant in the non-completion of the professional career. This analysis highlights the importance of using advanced Machine Learning models such as Random Forest to identify and mitigate critical factors that contribute to academic withdrawal, providing effective tools to improve retention and student success in higher education institutions.

articleTitle: Frequency Control for Audio Environments Using an Equalizer
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: In the realm of audio playback, a significant challenge persists: the limited ability to adapt the sound profile to individual preferences and the acoustic characteristics of different environments. To address this problem, this article presents the design of an equalization system capable of effectively managing the signals it processes. It details how audio control is achieved over different frequencies within the sound spectrum using bandpass filters with operational amplifiers for each of the 10 frequency bands. This allows for the independent adjustment of the amplitude of each frequency band. As a result, an efficient sound amplifier was achieved, capable of handling equalized signals without compromising sound quality.

articleTitle: Ecotoxicity in Teflon’s life cycle
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Teflon is a non-stick material used in a wide range of products, including cookware, clothing, and surface coatings. However, Teflon can negatively impact both the environment and human health. Its ecotoxicity is an important issue that must be addressed to protect the environment from global warming compounds and to prevent potential health risks, such as reproductive problems. Some substitutes for Teflon are now available that have less impact on the environment and human health, and they are affordable for everyone.

articleTitle: Security model with a holistic approach for mobile applications of financial entities in Colombia
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The increasing number of financial mobile applications, greater internet penetration, and enhanced internet capacity have created an attractive target for cybercriminals, as well as eliciting responses from the financial sector, authorities, and other entities.The proposal presented here is also a response to this increasingly complex scenario. The core of the proposal is to provide a holistic approach, supported by recognized standards and frameworks that either implicitly or explicitly apply this approach.This holistic approach is not an innovation, nor does it intend to be; it aims to ensure its application by considering all components related to the risks associated with the adoption of financial mobile applications in the Colombian environment and measures for their mitigation. It is neither prescriptive nor specific; it is general and functions as a framework that leads the user to consider elements that might be overlooked, ensuring that not only the human factor and technical aspects are taken into account but also going beyond the common explanation of how the human factor is the greatest vulnerability, which has been a long-standing distilled notion.

articleTitle: Preliminary evaluation of mechanical properties of recycled PET fiber reinforced concrete
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This paper presents the findings of an experimental study on the mechanical properties (compressive strength, flexural strength, tensile strength, and modulus of elasticity) of concrete reinforced with recycled PET fibers. The main goal of the research was to investigate the effect of recycled PET fiber addition into concrete on some mechanical properties of the material. PET fibers with a length of 55 mm were mixed into concrete by different amounts from 0 kg to 6 kg per m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. After that, tests of workability, modulus of elasticity, compressive, flexural strength, and tensile strength were made.The results indicate that the inclusion of PET fibers reduces the workability of fresh concrete, as evidenced by decreased slump values. However, PET fibers contribute to a lower apparent density and reduced water absorption and void percentages in the hardened concrete. Compressive strength tests revealed an optimal PET fiber content of approx. 2 kg per m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, which enhanced strength, while higher fiber contents led to a decline in performance. Flexural and splitting tensile strength tests demonstrated significant improvements with the addition of PET fibers.Overall, the study confirms that recycled PET fibers can effectively reinforce concrete, improving its mechanical properties while offering an innovative solution to plastic waste management. These findings support the integration of recycled PET fibers in construction practices, promoting environmental sustainability and advancing the development of eco-friendly building materials.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence: Applications, Advances in Weather Forecasting, and Emerging Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has evolved significantly since its inception, tracing its origins back to the mid-20th century with the ambition to simulate human intelligence. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of AI, beginning with its historical development. It explores AI’s applications across diverse industries, highlighting its transformative impact on healthcare, transportation, and entertainment. Specifically, it delves into AI’s role in revolutionizing weather forecasting by leveraging advanced algorithms to analyze meteorological data and predict weather patterns with unprecedented accuracy. Despite these advancements, the integration of AI presents notable challenges that must be addressed to improve AI performance.

articleTitle: Mobile Vehicle for Dosing Herbicides in Vegetable Crops
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The purpose of this document is to establish the design of a mobile vehicle for the dosage of herbicides in early phase vegetable crops, to automate the process, this need has arisen due to the damage caused to humans by toxic herbicides. The main objective is to analyze the primary parameters that make up a robotic platform, based on the physical and electrical characteristics presented by each of the stages (electronic, mechanical, power), representative in the mechatronic model.The result of the research focuses on determining the model and locomotion system for the optimal movement of the mobile platform and the control of movements in terrain that presents complex conditions for its trajectory, especially for applications of controlled robotic systems within the agricultural area.

articleTitle: Promoting Healthy Eating in Childhood: A Sustainable Business Project to Increase Vegetable Consumption Among Preschool and Middle-Aged Children through the Sustainable Business Model Canvas and 3-Phase Design Thinking in Metropolitan Lima
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Currently, children do not receive adequate nutrients from vegetables because they perceive them as having a poor presentation or taste. This is since some parents do not have the necessary time to prepare vegetable-based food products that are appealing to their children. As a result, children develop diseases such as obesity or anemia due to a lack of nutrients. To address this, a qualitative study is proposed to identify the need for increased vegetable consumption among children and the amount of time parents have available to prepare more elaborate meals. This will be carried out using the 3-phase Design Thinking (DT) approach to design a suitable value proposition for implementation within a Sustainable Business Model Canvas (BMCS) to create a nutritional, tasty, and sustainable food product by using fortified Andean cereals with vegetables through eco-friendly packaging. This way, parents will have a product that can be quickly cooked and provides nutrients to their children. Additionally, the product will be evaluated through hedonic tests to validate its acceptance by children.

articleTitle: Virtual assistant for the empowerment and business growth of Latin American women
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Summary - This article presents the implementation and evaluation of a virtual assistant developed under the Juntas Contamos, or We Count, program to empower and support women entrepreneurs in Latin America. Utilizing natural language processing technologies and recommendation systems, the assistant provides personalized information on financing and training. The results indicate a significant improvement in access to resources and the empowerment of female entrepreneurs, highlighting the potential of technological tools to foster business growth.

articleTitle: Analysis of PCI accuracy in flexible pavements using night images processed in Matlab
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Road safety is compromised by poor road conditions, which can trigger various types of accidents. It is essential to detect, and report affected areas to ensure the integrity and functionality of road infrastructure, facilitating fast and accurate actions. In this study, an innovative approach is adopted using night images processed with Matlab. In addition, histogram equalization is applied to improve the quality of the images, automatically adjusting the luminosity of the colors for a more accurate assessment of the faults. Experimental validation on a road in Chorrillos, Lima, demonstrates that the proposed model achieves an accuracy of over 97.2% in identifying damages, highlighting its performance in real conditions. This approach not only optimizes road maintenance, but also contributes significantly to the prevention and timely correction of situations that affect vehicular circulation.

articleTitle: Creating a calculator for engineers with a graphical interface using python
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: We present an advanced model of a calculator with a graphical user interface (GUI). By means of the programming language "Python" and the library "Tkinter", we developed a generous library of mathematical functions and algebraic algorithms that can be used by either an engineer or an undergraduate student to perform their basic calculations. Most functions and algorithms have been created from the ground up; instead of using the well-established functions and algorithms that can be found in libraries such as "numpy", "math", and "scipy.special", our own codes were used to implement them. In fact, our functions provide the user additional alternatives like allowing him or her to choose the desired approximation level and generate a visual help menu that explains the syntax of each algorithm. While some of the algorithms are more time-efficient than those found in the regular python libraries, our main contribution is the creation of a GUI that is very user-friendly and can be extended and optimized according to the needs and expectations of the programmer.

articleTitle: The Corona Effect and its Impact in the Communication Bands at Frequencies Below 1000 MHZ
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This study investigates the corona effect in high voltage transmission lines and its impact on telecommunications systems operating in the 30 MHz to 1 GHz frequency range. The study aims to develop a comprehensive model using data from previous investigations, reconstructing the characteristics of the corona effect and analyze its influence on voice, data, and television services, as well as IoT and radar systems using a mathematical model. Understanding and mitigating the adverse effects of corona-induced noise and interference will enhance the reliability and performance of these communication systems.

articleTitle: The influence of Inbound Marketing and the PDCA cycle on the adoption of best practices for customer loyalty in a retail SME
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This article analyzes the influence of Inbound Marketing and the PDCA cycle (Plan, Do, Check, Act) on the adoption of best practices for customer loyalty in a small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) in the retail sector. Inbound Marketing, focused on attracting and retaining customers through relevant content, is combined with the PDCA cycle, which seeks to continuously improve processes. The implementation of these strategies allows the SME to develop a customer-centric approach, adapting to their needs and generating loyalty through the delivery of value. This study highlights the importance of these practices in customer loyalty within the context of the retail sector. The results showed that the combination of these two strategies enabled the company to improve its ability to attract and retain customers, as well as to adapt agilely to the changing needs and preferences of the market.

articleTitle: Methodologies for the design of semi-rigid pavements with granular materials treated with cement: a review
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The use of granular materials treated with cement MGTC increases the structural capacity and durability of pavements. The design of pavements using these materials contemplates fatigue damage in the asphalt mix, cracking of the MGTC and rutting in the subgrade. This document aims to analyze the methodologies used for the design of flexible pavements considering MGTC. To this end, the math fundamentals, procedures and formulations of the Australian methodology (AUSTROADS), South African Pavement Design Method (SAMDM) and American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) are exposed. Likewise, the criteria used by the Urban Development Institute IDU for the city of Bogotá in Colombia are exposed. From the bibliographic review carried out, the authors present some comments and suggestions for the design of pavements in Colombia.

articleTitle: Exploring Lean Construction and BIM benefits in a SMEs: an office remodeling project
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The construction industry is characterized by low productivity, cost overruns and project delays. In recent years, the implementation of Lean Construction and BIM (Building Information Modeling) are helping to mitigate these problems, with a large number of applications worldwide. However, research on the implementation of Lean Construction and BIM in SMEs (Small Medium Enterprises) is scarce. That is why the following article aims to show the application of Lean and BIM in an office remodeling project in Peru, establishing a methodology that involves value management, planning, information management and change management, using lean tools such as Last Planner System, Choosing By Advantages, the Big room, among others. As a result, the implementation provided benefits such as: improvement of value delivery, improvement of the time to collect observations, improvement of stakeholder satisfaction and improvement of information management. The following work will be of help to professionals in the construction sector belonging to SMEs that wish to implement Lean and BIM.

articleTitle: Service Level Improvement Of An SME In The Peruvian Textile Sector Using Lean Manufacturing Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This study delves into the main factors that contribute to service delays within a medium-sized textile company in Peru. The methodology was structured into three consecutive components, starting with the company diagnosis, then the design evaluation where standardization, 5S, and TPM were implemented. Finally, the improvement was validated with the Arena software. The results of this research underline the positive impact of the service level on the company by achieving an increase from 68.75% to 74.6%, due to the number of complete orders delivered on time. Additionally, the implementation of the 5S tool improved the efficiency of shirt production by minimizing search times. Going from 73.79, to 82.41 garments per man hour. The standardization achieved in the project increased from 20% to 75% after creating cleaning manuals, checklists, and order and cleaning policies. Preventive maintenance when reducing machine downtime caused by unforeseen failures. The OEE was achieved from 80.05% to 98.11%. This research seeks to improve the service level of an SME company by identifying the root causes of service delays, the research seeks to empower the company to achieve operational excellence and provide exceptional customer service.

articleTitle: Development of a simplification methodology for the design of reinforced concrete buildings up to 10 stories
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This article presents a simplification methodology for the design of reinforced concrete buildings up to 10 stories in Peru, addressing the lack of specific guidelines in the E.060 code. The methodology, based on national and international standards, includes restrictions and guidelines to ensure structural regularity, optimized cross-sectional shapes, and adequate seismic resistance. The analyses conducted show a reduction in design complexity and time while meeting safety standards, and comparisons with conventional designs reveal benefits in efficiency and costs. Moreover, the methodology is presented with practical examples and case studies, highlighting its usefulness as a validation tool for designers. This approach not only optimizes the design process but also promotes standardization and consistency in outcomes, enhancing the competitiveness and sustainability of projects in Peru's construction market.

articleTitle: State of the Art in Software-Defined Networks: A Practical View
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This article provides a comprehensive and practical overview of the evolution and current state of Software-Defined Networking (SDN). It delves into the origins of SDN, its core principles, and key milestones in its development, including the advent and advancements of OpenFlow. The study examines the expansion of SDN into wide-area and wireless networks and explores the adoption of hybrid models that combine SDN with other networking paradigms. Furthermore, it investigates the latest trends in SDN, such as network slicing, security considerations, and integration with emerging technologies. This article seeks to provide significant insights to scholars, professionals, and decision-makers in comprehending the revolutionary influence of SDN and its prospects.

articleTitle: Machine learning algorithms in the detection of anemia in children under 5 years of age in southern Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The present study focuses on the challenge of identifying anemia in children under 5 years of age. in the departments of Cusco, Moquegua, Puno, Tacna and Arequipa, considered as the southern zone of Peru. The importance of early detection of this disease is highlighted due to the irreversible consequences. The main objective is to apply and compare the various Machine Learning algorithms for the early detection of this disease. The aim is to evaluate the effectiveness of the KNN, Decision Tree and Naïve Bayes models, in order to identify the most accurate algorithm. A dataset from the Information System of the Nutritional Status of Children and Pregnant Women Peru (SIEN) was used, including variables such as sex, age in months, weight, height, hemoglobin, among others. Data cleaning and processing techniques were applied to prepare them for the use of the different Machine Learning algorithms. The results obtained show high accuracy rates of the algorithms used, the algorithms with the highest precision were Decision Tree and KNN with 99.21% and 96.56% respectively. In addition, Naïve Bayes showed remarkable performance with an accuracy of 94.94%. Based on the comparisons of accuracy rates, it is concluded that the most effective algorithm for the early detection of anemia in children in southern Peru is Decision Tree.

articleTitle: Methodology for Launching Sustainable Business Models Based on the Value Proposition Canvas and the Sustainable Business Model Canvas in a Second-Hand Clothing Venture
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to improve the value proposition foundation before launching sustainable business models. The main problem is the lack of equitable distribution in the importance of the three axes of sustainability applied to a business: economic, environmental, and social. Increasingly, ventures with sustainable pillars are required that not only have the profit axis as the main one but also go equitably according to the environmental and social axes corresponding to their line of business. To achieve this, it is important to start by applying new methodologies to traditional value propositions, so that they can be truly useful when applied to sustainable business models of any kind. Therefore, this article will develop a methodology based on the Sustainable Business Model Canvas and the Value Proposition Canvas. In this way, it seeks to increase the sustainable impact of new business models entering the market.

articleTitle: Prismatica: A physical computing prototype for color theory
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Exploring Color Theory: A Journey Through Creative Chromatics addresses the fundamental principles of color theory and its application in creative fields. The theory is based on concepts and relationships that influence color perception, being crucial for artists and designers. Two main models, additive (RGB) and subtractive (CMY) synthesis, are essential to understanding the creation and combination of colors. PRISMÁTICA is a project, which integrates color theory and technology, offers an HCI through the physical computing, for an educational experience that facilitates the practical understanding of color mixing. PRISMÁTICA stands out for its educational interactivity, the practical application of knowledge, technological innovation and pedagogical potential.

articleTitle: Digital Marketing Model through Inbound Marketing to enhance brand positioning in a veterinary clinic
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The article focuses on the veterinary sector, which has experienced robust growth and the emergence of new competitors. In Peru, there are approximately 4950 veterinary clinics, with 50% of them concentrated in Lima, increasingly competing to retain and attract new clients. Social media has become an efficient means to interact with and capture the attention of users. This research aims in the short term to increase reactions and followers on social media, and in the medium term, to achieve the loyalty and conversion of users into loyal customers to the brand. Considering the evidence, implementing a digital marketing model on social media based on inbound marketing is required. This will optimize the presence and positioning of a veterinary clinic's brand, generating greater customer loyalty and sales opportunities.

articleTitle: Mortar Properties with Glass Powder and Fly Ash: A Study on Sustainability and Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The substitution of cement in cement-based materials, such as concrete and mortar mixes, is considered an attractive alternative for future construction materials due to the high CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions produced during their manufacture. This study evaluated the feasibility of incorporating glass powder and fly ash into mortar production as partial substitutes for ordinary Portland cement, aiming to reduce carbon emissions and promote sustainability in the construction sector. Manually crushed colored glass powder, general-purpose Portland cement, and fly ash were used as binders. A Design of Experiments approach and Response Surface Methodology (RSM) were employed to analyze changes in mortar properties. The objective was to maintain or improve the compressive strength and workability of the mortar mixes. The results demonstrated that the water-to-binder ratio had a greater impact on workability compared to the percentage of glass powder. Lower values of glass powder resulted in higher compressive strength. The optimal mix included a 0.55 water-to-binder ratio and 5% glass powder, achieving workability of 131.86 and compressive strength of 20.88 MPa. This study provides insights into the potential of using supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) to create more sustainable and environmentally friendly construction materials while maintaining desired mechanical properties.

articleTitle: Application of Scrumban in the execution of single-family homes in Lima, Peru to optimize construction times
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Currently, the construction industry predominantly employs traditional methodology as a project management framework due to the sequential nature of construction. However, this methodology does not focus much on delivering value to the customer. Faced with such issues, the software industry adopted agile methodology many years ago as a project management system. While the construction industry is constantly seeking continuous improvement and good communication with clients, there is limited information on applying agile methodology as a solution to the customer value delivery problem. Precisely, the Scrumban framework is an alternative solution that enhances team communication and improves activity planning through a dynamic board that visualizes the tasks to be performed according to customer requirements. In this article, Scrumban is adapted to a single-family housing project to optimize execution time, as timely project delivery was central to the customer. Thus, considering the SPI (Schedule Performance Index) metric, an improvement from 0.81 to 0.87 in work progress was achieved, and delays in construction were mitigated, resulting in a 1-day advancement compared to the planned schedule.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of the implementation of organic coagulant derived from sugarcane bagasse for the removal of scale in pipes
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Water is the basic resource to guarantee the life of all living beings on the planet. Access to water, sanitation and hygiene is a fundamental right, yet billions of people around the world continue to face enormous difficulties every day in accessing the most basic services. The objective on this work was investigates the efficacy of an eco-friendly coagulant derived from sugarcane bagasse in mitigating mineral scale deposition in piping systems. Comparative tests were conducted between this organic coagulant and conventional chemical coagulants such as aluminum sulfate and ferric chloride. The results demonstrated that the sugarcane bagasse-derived coagulant exhibits a scale removal efficiency comparable to that of traditional chemical coagulants, while offering additional benefits of environmental friendliness and reduced infrastructure damage. The study concludes that the use of this organic coagulant is a viable and sustainable alternative, potentially lowering operational costs in water treatment processes. Further research is recommended to standardize production and assess

articleTitle: Feasibility and application of Last Planner System 2.0 in Harzone Modular Bridge projects to reduce incidents and inconveniences in execution in Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This study focuses on the feasibility and application of Last Planner System 2.0 in the scheduling and execution of modular bridges in Peru, highlighting the importance and distinction of an appropriate control and follow-up management to minimize incidents. The most significant parameters concern the integration and sequencing of Takt planning principles, the critical path method (CPM), phased planning and Lookahead to optimize the management of time, resources and uninterrupted workflow. A comparative study was conducted between pre- and post-implementation periods and analysis of LPS 2.0 on modular bridge projects, revealing significant improvements in the development of weekly plans and a notable reduction in the variability of the Percentage of Plan Completed (PPC). Implementation results demonstrate significant improvements, incidents were reduced by 77.41% from 29 to 8 incidents, incident response time was reduced to 57.14%, and additional costs were reduced by 64.28%. In addition, compliance with the execution deadlines (PPC) increased from 69.81% to 93.39%. The values obtained support the efficiency and adaptability of the tools used, contributing to the fulfillment of planned activities. The improvement in the processes is reflected in a cost reduction accompanied by a better workflow and compliance with deadlines in the various stages of construction of Harzone type modular bridges.

articleTitle: Implementation of Lean Manufacturing and SLP in an SME in the jewelry sector: Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Peru, despite being a mining country, does not represent one of the largest jewelry exporters worldwide. Likewise, jewelry SMEs present problems regarding delivery times, due to delays in the production process, causing a failure to meet the delivery date agreed upon with the client. Therefore, the following field study arises to improve compliance with delivery times in a jewelry SME. The main objective is the optimization of production processes by eliminating non-added value activities and redistributing the journey of operators by applying 5S, SMED and SLP tools and using VSM analysis tools, Pareto diagram, Ishikawa diagram. The results obtained showed an increase of 43.2% in the 5s evaluation matrix. The total reduction in travel distance was 115.76 meters using the SLP tool. Finally, a 30.32% reduction in set-up times with the SMED tool. Therefore, a reduction in production process time was obtained by 117.01 minutes, contributing to an improvement in delivery times.

articleTitle: Health and Environmental Education in Communities in Highly Vulnerable Situation. Case Study: San Luis, San Isidro Patios – La Calera, Colombia
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Educational constructivism emphasizes the interaction between the individual and the environment to build knowledge, prioritizing social collaboration and personal reflection. In the San Luis sector of San Isidro Patios, a participatory educational model is proposed to address the lack and consumption of poor-quality water. The methodology, divided into five phases, seeks to optimize the transfer of knowledge through human interaction and the combination of pedagogical approaches.The instructional design follows nine steps, from the definition of problems to the selection of teaching resources, adapting to the student and the community context. Constructivist, cognitivist, and behaviorist approaches are integrated, highlighting situated learning and formative assessment to promote effective and participatory instruction. The workshops focus on acquiring skills to address problems such as the lack of drinking water and inefficient rainwater collection systems in homes.Specific objectives, student considerations, content analysis, teaching strategies and objective evaluation are an integral part of the design, which includes learning units and teaching-learning approaches adapted to each type of knowledge. Teaching strategies include communication, group work and practical workshops, with evaluation criteria that consider viability, environmental responsibility, social inclusion, innovation and technical feasibility.The educational approach adopted seeks to promote community participation in solving real problems related to water supply and management. The importance of considering the specific characteristics of the target community and the integration of complementary pedagogical models is highlighted. The methodology seeks not only to address the problem of water supply, but also to empower participants through a participatory educational process oriented towards concrete solutions.

articleTitle: Improvement of Productivity in SMEs of the Textile Sector through Lean Manufacturing: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The present study was conducted within a textile workshop situated within the manufacturing sector of the Peruvian textile industry. Numerous challenges impact the productivity of small and medium-sized enterprises in this sector, including extended periods of inactivity, reprocessing, and substandard quality, among others; the primary aim of this research is to enhance productivity in accordance with the industry benchmark of 0.13 units per PEN. A production model incorporating the Standardized Work, 5S, SLP, and Poka-Yoke methodologies was implemented as part of the proposed solution. Simulation of the present state and the enhanced state was subsequently accomplished utilizing the Arena software. Arena application. Furthermore, it was demonstrated that the suggested model increased output by as much as 0.11 percentage points, decreased cycle time to 318 minutes, and enhanced effort (kg-m), which totaled 349 kg-m. Ultimately, this study was conducted to aid in the expansion of the industry and serve as a benchmark for businesses employing comparable procedures seeking to enhance efficiency.

articleTitle: Lessons Learned to reduce impacts of COVID-19 in construction projects: the case of Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has generated several impacts on the construction sector such as project delays, cost overruns, among others. However, despite its impacts, little research has focused on compiling lessons learned to mitigate the impacts on the construction sector. Therefore, this research aims to compile the main strategies taken by professionals in the construction sector to mitigate the impacts of COVID-19 in the construction sector. For this, the research starts with a literature review of the impacts of COVID-19 and 110 professionals are surveyed about the impact of COVID-19 in Peruvian construction projects and the impacts are classified using RII (Relative Importance Index); based on the impacts, a literature review of mitigation strategies is carried out and six Peruvian experts are consulted about the adapted strategies, the main adapted strategies were the adoption of safety and health measures, implementation of Lean Construction. This research will be a contribution for professionals in the construction sector to the extent that they can make better decisions in the face of possible events with high variability and uncertainty such as COVID-19 that may occur in the future.

articleTitle: Proposal to improve road safety by implementing minor interventions using the ViDA-iRAP software
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Currently, injuries resulting from traffic accidents result in the death of around 1.19 million people per year worldwide [1]. Therefore, road safety is a critical component of urban and rural development, especially in developing countries. The implementation of minor interventions can result in significant improvements without incurring high costs. This article proposes a series of measures to improve road safety using the assessment provided by the International Road Assessment Programme (iRAP). Above all, its ViDA-iRAP software is an effective tool for identifying risks and proposing appropriate solutions, since it has a "star" rating (safety measures) where one star represents the worst case and five stars represent the best case for both road infrastructure and pedestrians, with the aim of establishing measures to reduce the large number of deaths and serious injuries that are currently occurring in countries due to road safety issues. The research carried out by Cayao and Ferreyra will be evaluated on the data obtained from the modeling with the software, how the program assessed the improvement results showing significant changes, and the problem of the large flow of motorcycle taxis on the road will be seen.

articleTitle: Feasibility of using an optimized system in the management of change control in plans to improve the communication system between those involved
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: This research addresses the improvement of communication to prevent interference in plans for small-medium sized multi-family housing projects. Based on this problem, the need to innovate and improve efficiency, adapting it to new technologies, is evident. To this end, an optimized system is proposed through the use of Odei.io, which centralizes information, allows real-time monitoring of the project and facilitates collaboration between specialties. It should be noted that the research is based on a theoretical approach and is validated through the judgment of experts in the real estate project construction sector, whose results together demonstrate the viability of the proposal and the predisposition for its implementation in projects of this type.

articleTitle: Current advances about the use of nanosilica in self-compacting concrete: An overview of the mechanical and durability properties
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: Self-compacting concrete (SCC) is a modern construction material that, due to its good fresh characteristics of passing ability, filling ability, and segregation and bleeding resistance, this can fill complex forms with limited accessibility and congested reinforcement, and it consolidates under its own weight without any vibration. On the other hand, nanosilica is considered the most widely used nanomaterial in the construction industry, and recently has become used to enhance the SCC properties. However, the use of nanosilica and its effects on the mechanical and durability properties of SCC has not been fully understood and exploited by the construction sector. For this reason, the current work presents a brief state of the art about outstanding worldwide research over the last 5 years dealing with the mechanical and durability properties of the SCC modified by nanosilica. The recent studies accessed state that nanosilica enhances by up to 60%, 28%, 60%, 13%, 28%, 80%, 75%, 825%, 93% and 5.3%, respectively, the compressive strength, tensile strength, flexural strength, elastic modulus, fracture resistance, chloride penetration resistance, sulfate and acid resistance, corrosion resistance, water absorption resistance, and the shrinkage resistance of the SCC. Conversely, the recent studies report that nanosilica increases the risk of carbonation of the SCC by up to 23%. Furthermore, the recent studies allow to identify that the optimal nanosilica dosage that further improves the mechanical and durability performances of the SCC can be set at 2–3 wt.%, but more research is needed about the nanosilica effect on the carbonation, corrosion, and the structural performance of the reinforced SCC. Based on these identified outputs, benefits and limitations of the nanosilica are addressed, and recommendations about their implementation in the SCC are provided to carry out further performance and case studies.

articleTitle: Designing a value proposition based on Lean Startup and Scrum for creating a beverage made from Amazonian fruits sweetened with Yacon syrup
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: In Peru, excessive consumption of sugary beverages has emerged as a growing public health issue. This phenomenon is associated with an increase in chronic diseases such as obesity and diabetes, negatively impacting the population's well-being and generating a significant economic burden on the healthcare system. This article develops a combinatorial model that links two approaches: Lean Startup and Scrum, in 5 phases, with the purpose of creating a value proposition. The main result of this research supports the effectiveness of merging Lean Startup and Scrum in successfully addressing the market need. Problem validation demonstrates that 87.5% of respondents identified excessive consumption of sugary beverages as a significant issue. The questionnaire also confirmed a marked interest in the beverage, with 87% willing to try it and 68% interested in tasting events. The main conclusion highlights that the research has fulfilled its motivation by demonstrating the viability of the value proposition and the effectiveness of combining the methodologies.

articleTitle: Process Capability Evaluation on Timing Surgery Scheduling in an Odontology Colombian Clinic. An analysis from Six Sigma
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The article presents the results of the analysis of the process capability evaluation in surgery scheduling in a Colombian Odontology Clinic using Lean Six Sigma (LSS) to establish improvement projects. Scheduling supports the whole surgery procedure in healthcare facilities due to the importance of estimating resources for medical assistance and optimizing the available time. LSS is a widely known methodology for improving processes, and its applications in healthcare are related to the importance of increasing the value added to the Patient Safety Policy. The methodology consists of applying the DMAIC cycle. The covered tools focus on reducing the waiting time for surgery scheduling, identifying its causes, and establishing improvements. The case study did not have evidence of previous LSS methodology applications, but it had implemented a quality management system. The results showed that the process lacks control due to the process capability, and the causes are associated with errors in the application of procedures, diagnostic and improvement actions. The business case does not use previous inputs such as diagnosis (dental x-rays) and surgery complications for scheduling the surgeries, and the process has no indicators clearly defined, so this is an opportunity to determine leading causes of time extension and to schedule the surgery appropriately. Future studies could be related to establishing improvements, controlling those in the process, and training the involved people.

articleTitle: Low-Compute Cryptography for IoT: Challenges, Solutions, and Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, projected to reach 75 billion by 2025, presents unprecedented security challenges. This paper explores the critical issues in implementing robust cryptographic solutions for IoT systems, characterized by severe resource constraints, energy limitations, and unique vulnerabilities. We examine the key challenges, including the implementation of standard cryptographic algorithms on devices with as little as 32 KB flash memory and 2 KB RAM, the energy consumption of cryptographic operations in battery-powered devices, and the latency issues in time-critical applications. The paper also addresses the scalability problems of traditional public key infrastructures in the context of billions of IoT devices and the susceptibility of these devices to physical and side-channel attacks.Furthermore, we present justifications for research into low-computation cryptographic schemes tailored for IoT. This includes recent advancements in lightweight cryptographic algorithms, the potential of elliptic curve cryptography for resource-constrained environments, and emerging techniques like partial homomorphic encryption for real-time applications. The paper also discusses the exploration of blockchain technology as a decentralized alternative to traditional PKI and the ongoing efforts in standardizing post-quantum algorithms for IoT.Finally, we consider the broader implications of this research, including its economic impact, the need for global IoT security standards, and the convergence with other emerging technologies like AI and 5G. This comprehensive review underscores the critical importance of developing robust, efficient cryptographic solutions for IoT as a cornerstone of security, privacy, and economic progress in the digital era.

articleTitle: Competency-Based BIM Curriculum Proposal: The Case of a Peruvian University
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The global implementation of BIM (Building Information Modeling) has led many countries to propose projects that adapt to the new trends because its application improves productivity and collaboration in projects. However, few studies focus on the implementation of BIM in the pedagogical field, as this is an essential field for the training of future professionals in the AEC industry. Therefore, the following study aims to propose a BIM competency-based curriculum for the Peruvian market. The research begins with an identification of BIM competencies for the Peruvian market, based on national BIM studies and continues with a literature review of curricula, where 20 international curricula were identified, based on which a competency-based curriculum adapting BIM is proposed for the Academic Professional School of Civil Engineering of the Universidad Continental. The following research will be a contribution both for professionals because it identifies the key competencies for BIM implementation in the Peruvian market and for academics who wish to implement BIM in their curricula.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Communication Support Technologies for people with disabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The article investigates the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Communication Support Technologies (CST) for people with disabilities. It explores AI applications such as voice recognition, natural language processing, and machine learning to improve communication and accessibility. The research highlights significant advances in CST, showing how these emerging technologies transform communication and access to information. Additionally, the benefits and possibilities of personalized and effective communication tools are discussed, and future research areas that could further expand AI's positive impact on CST are suggested, promoting equal opportunities and social inclusion.

articleTitle: Improvement proposal to increase the level of service by applying Lean Manufacturing tools in SMEs in the textile sector in Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The Peruvian economy is sustained by several industries. The textile industry is an area that generates a high impact on it, in addition to generating many jobs. However, nowadays the customer is more demanding, so companies are committed to improving their products. As a result, there is a gap between companies and the market. Currently, they have experienced low efficiency in the companies' processes related to the level of service, non-fulfillment of orders and defective products. As a result, opportunities for improvement generate a waste of resources. This article presents a technical proposal that leverages Lean Manufacturing principles, specifically Poka-Yoke and Kanban tools, alongside established Quality Policies, to enhance service level performance. Utilizing data collected from the case study company, Arena software was employed to simulate both the current operational state and a proposed improved scenario. Through this simulation, a demonstrably significant 15% improvement in service level rate was achieved. Finally, the contribution of this study can help other companies related to the textile sector regarding the application of Lean Manufacturing tools together with Quality Policies achieving a better management of resources.

articleTitle: Study of the Heterogeneous Catalytic Model for Syngas Production in a Simulated Environment for Application in CO2 Capture Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Congreso Internacional de Innovación y Tendencias en Ingeniería (CONIITI)
abstract: The study was carried out under the possibility of transforming conventional petrochemical processes, such as ammonia production plant, into carbon dioxide capture systems by means of replacing fossil natural gas with biogas, generated by manure during an anaerobic digestion. Three partial substitution scenarios were pro- posed: 30, 40 and 50% in order to analyse the behaviour of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the syngas unit process, applying an equivalent CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> balance to evaluate if it is possible to capture this GHG within the same process, thus achieving negative emissions.
